strengths: Addresses an important question: what latent information multimodal contrastive learning recovers when modalities contain related but nonidentical factors.

The simple CLIP postprocessing pipeline shows practical promise across multiple encoders and datasets. For example, Table 2 reports an improvement in ViT-B/16 average target accuracy from 32.51% to 37.13%.
Synthetic experiments explore assumption violations with repeated runs. Appendix P adds ground-truth Multimodal3DIdent evaluation, reporting image/text recovery R² of 0.97/0.75.
weaknesses: The central proof relies on an incorrect result (Appendix D.1, Lemma 2). The claimed optimum L−2logN=0 is the collapsed/chance value; informative encoders can achieve negative values. More fundamentally, requiring paired embeddings to coincide almost surely under the full-support vMF coupling forces constant embeddings, contradicting the simultaneous uniformity requirement. Consequently, the elimination of modality-specific variables and equality of encoder mappings used by Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 are not established. This is a fundamental soundness issue.

The convex-body argument contains an additional substantive error. Equation (43) substitutes an exactly uniform p(z_t), whereas Lemma 3 only claims convergence to uniformity as λ approaches zero. At finite λ, normalized distance kernels on bounded domains generally induce nonuniform marginals, invalidating the stated cross-entropy identity. Furthermore, Corollary 2 is stated for general norms, but Appendix E.2 requires Lα geometry with α≠2; Euclidean balls permit arbitrary rotations rather than only scaled permutations.

The FastICA guarantee conflicts with the hyperspherical assumptions (Section 5 and Appendix O). Uniform spherical variables have dependent Cartesian coordinates and rotational symmetry, so ICA cannot identify privileged independent source coordinates under this model. Counting M−1 degrees of freedom does not resolve this incompatibility. The proposed local-isometry justification for applying PCA and ICA to CLIP also remains heuristic.

The downstream experiments do not isolate disentanglement from whitening and dimensionality reduction. Appendix K uses 300 components for ICA versus 160–200 for PCA+ICA, without matched PCA-only or whitening controls. At fixed whitened features, an orthogonal ICA rotation leaves the optimally trained L2-regularized linear-probe problem unchanged. Thus the reported accuracy gains do not establish that recovering independent components causes the improvement.

The direct recovery evidence has important limitations. Appendix K regresses learned representations on true latents; high R² can therefore occur for a rank-deficient projection that discards latent factors. Appendix P provides useful additional R² results but lacks componentwise recovery comparisons and sufficient training/evaluation details. Selected CelebA traversals and counts of visually identified attributes are insufficient quantitative validation of disentanglement. Downstream results also lack uncertainty estimates.

The causal novelty is insufficiently established. The analysis models statistical coupling but does not formally demonstrate that its restrictive parameterizations capture the motivating mixtures of opposing causal mechanisms. Much of the identifiability machinery is inherited from Zimmermann et al. (2021), making the invalid multimodal bridge especially consequential. The practical preprocessing results cannot compensate for unsupported central theoretical claims.
